bull_bear.body:
- Global branded specialty innovation model — Ryaltris®, Glenmark's first globally launched branded specialty product, scaled through proprietary R&D plus a partnership-led commercialization model to 56 countries, ranking among the top 3 brands in 17 markets and #1 in 5 markets.
- Proprietary biologics/multispecific-antibody R&D platform (IGI's BEAT® protein platform), validated externally by a landmark licensing agreement with AbbVie for ISB 2001 (USD 700 Mn upfront; potential aggregate deal value USD 1.925 Bn).
- Diversified, balanced geographic and therapy-area mix (India, North America, Europe, Emerging Markets; Dermatology, Respiratory, Oncology, Cardiac, Diabetes) that reduces dependence on any single market or therapy.
- Strong brand equity and market position in India — ranked 2nd in Dermatology, 3rd in Respiratory and 4th in Cardiac (IQVIA MAT Mar'26), with 11 brands among the IPM Top 300 and secondary-sales growth consistently outperforming the IPM.
- Broad R&D infrastructure of six centres (Sinnar, Taloja, Mahape, Lausanne, New York, Neuchâtel) supporting a pipeline spanning specialty branded products, generics and biologics.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Pharmaceutical R&D and pipeline execution risk — The AR flags the 'inherent uncertainty associated with pharmaceutical R&D' as a key risk (categorized as Financial Risk, Strategic Risk): the discovery-to-commercialization journey is lengthy and involves scientific, regulatory, manufacturing and commercial challenges at every stage, and not all development programs will achieve regulatory approval or commercial success, which may affect future revenue generation.
- Product quality risk — Ensuring product quality across manufacturing, packaging, labeling and distribution is identified as essential to consumer trust and brand reputation; the AR states that any instance of failure in product quality would have serious repercussions, particularly as the Company introduces new products and expands into new markets (categorized as Quality Risk).
- U.S. antitrust and consumer-protection litigation — Glenmark USA continued to defend multiple antitrust and consumer protection lawsuits relating to industry-wide allegations of price-fixing, market allocation and related conduct; it agreed to separate settlements of USD 37.75 Mn with the putative direct purchaser class and USD 29.63 Mn with state attorneys general (the latter payable in annual installments over five years), subject to court approval, while denying the underlying allegations.
- U.S. FDA regulatory and manufacturing-site inspection risk — The Monroe, North Carolina formulations facility required a U.S. FDA Establishment Inspection Report before commercial manufacturing could restart (resolved with a Voluntary Action Indicated classification in November 2025), illustrating exposure to FDA site-inspection outcomes. As of March 31, 2026 the Company also had 52 applications pending at various stages of the U.S. FDA approval process, including 25 Paragraph IV applications, an unresolved regulatory-approval pipeline.
- Geopolitical and demand-volatility exposure in Emerging Markets — Emerging Markets (Russia/CIS, LATAM, MEA, APAC) performance in FY2026 was affected by seasonal demand patterns, geopolitical uncertainties and delayed launches in selected markets, particularly in the first half, indicating structural exposure to geopolitical and macro volatility across the Company's international footprint.
- India regulatory/tax-policy transition sensitivity — The August 2025 GST regime change caused a pronounced one-time impact to India formulation sales in Q2 FY2026, contributing to a reported 17.0% decline in India business revenue for FY2026 despite strong underlying secondary-sales demand, showing sensitivity to domestic tax-policy transitions.
- Enterprise-wide geopolitical and scientific-advancement complexity — Glenmark's risk governance disclosure states that, as a pharmaceutical company with a global geographic footprint, it is 'inherently exposed to a diverse set of risks including geopolitical complexity and scientific advancements,' managed through an Enterprise Risk Management Framework overseen by the Board's Risk Management Committee.

business.body: The Company specializes in research & development, manufacturing, and sales of a diverse range of pharmaceutical products, including branded generics, generics, specialty medications, and over-the-counter (OTC) treatments, spanning dermatology, respiratory health, oncology, cardiology, diabetes, gynecology, gastroenterology, and anti-infectives. Its global formulation business runs across Branded, Generics and OTC segments in India, North America, Europe and Emerging Markets (Russia/CIS, Latin America, Middle East & Africa, Asia-Pacific), serving healthcare professionals, hospitals, government wholesalers, distributors and retail pharmacies through its own subsidiaries and third-party distributors.

business.title: Group structure (profile)

business.body:
- Global branded specialty innovation model — Ryaltris®, Glenmark's first globally launched branded specialty product, scaled through proprietary R&D plus a partnership-led commercialization model to 56 countries, ranking among the top 3 brands in 17 markets and #1 in 5 markets.
- Proprietary biologics/multispecific-antibody R&D platform (IGI's BEAT® protein platform), validated externally by a landmark licensing agreement with AbbVie for ISB 2001 (USD 700 Mn upfront; potential aggregate deal value USD 1.925 Bn).
- Diversified, balanced geographic and therapy-area mix (India, North America, Europe, Emerging Markets; Dermatology, Respiratory, Oncology, Cardiac, Diabetes) that reduces dependence on any single market or therapy.
- Strong brand equity and market position in India — ranked 2nd in Dermatology, 3rd in Respiratory and 4th in Cardiac (IQVIA MAT Mar'26), with 11 brands among the IPM Top 300 and secondary-sales growth consistently outperforming the IPM.
- Broad R&D infrastructure of six centres (Sinnar, Taloja, Mahape, Lausanne, New York, Neuchâtel) supporting a pipeline spanning specialty branded products, generics and biologics.
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Moving up the value chain through leadership in three global therapeutic areas — Dermatology, Respiratory, and Oncology — by scaling differentiated products, expanding specialty platforms, and advancing proprietary and partnered innovation.
- Advancing innovation and specialty: continuing to scale proprietary innovation (Ryaltris®) globally, expanding the innovative Oncology portfolio across India and Emerging Markets through partnerships, building Specialty Dermatology and Respiratory portfolios across Europe, and continuing investment in IGI's proprietary BEAT® platform for next-generation multispecific antibodies.
- Scaling the branded business: increasing the contribution of branded markets and products — strengthening the branded business in India, expanding scale across Emerging Markets through deeper penetration and regional brands, and increasing branded/specialty contribution in Europe led by Respiratory and Dermatology.
- Building a generics business: scaling the U.S. generics business through Respiratory and Injectable launches, expanding the U.S. Injectables portfolio across hospital/institutional channels, pursuing selective first-to-file opportunities, and gaining scale in Europe generics while progressively increasing higher-value product contribution.
- Nurturing sustainability: embedding sustainability into operations and growth, advancing SBTi validation, TNFD disclosure, human rights and workplace culture, and integrating environmental/social considerations into business decisions.
- Creating sustainable shareholder value: driving profitable growth and superior returns through disciplined capital allocation, portfolio enhancement, and operating leverage; prioritizing growth initiatives with shorter payback periods; maintaining working capital structurally below the industry average; and pursuing selective, ROCE-gated CAPEX and M&A.
- Expanding strategic partnerships across the innovation lifecycle — in-licensing differentiated therapies to strengthen priority therapeutic areas, and partnering IGI-originated innovation with global biopharmaceutical leaders to accelerate development, expand reach and unlock pipeline value.
- Oncology franchise build-out: scaling the oncology franchise across India and Emerging Markets through innovative product launches and stronger commercial capabilities, and advancing next-generation oncology innovation through IGI's multispecific pipeline.
- Respiratory strategy: scaling Ryaltris® as a global growth platform, strengthening the respiratory portfolio across Europe and North America, and building U.S. leadership through differentiated respiratory generics and device-led capabilities.
- Dermatology strategy: sustaining leadership in India and Emerging Markets while expanding into higher-value specialty opportunities, scaling Winlevi® across Europe, and strengthening prescription and OTC/DTC dermatology portfolios in select markets.
- Capital allocation decisions — including annual operating plans, business strategies, capital expenditure proposals and quarterly/half-yearly/annual financial results — are reviewed and approved by the Board of Directors, with the Audit Committee reviewing financial statements and key financial reporting matters before Board consideration. Dividend recommendations are approved by the Board and put to a shareholder vote at the AGM; a dividend of INR 2.50 per equity share for FY2026 was placed before Members for approval at the 48th AGM.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: North America: continued build-out of the injectable portfolio (more than 20 injectable products launched to date), first-to-market Respiratory generic launches (first to launch the generic version of FloVent® 44 mcg in the U.S.), and an OTC private-label business expanded to seven clients in FY2026. Europe: direct commercial presence expanded to 13 markets with 8 new Respiratory product launches in FY2026, and the launch of Winlevi® (Glenmark's first New Chemical Entity) in the UK followed by EU marketing authorization, providing a platform for further expansion across Glenmark's licensed European territories in FY2027. Emerging Markets: Glenmark is building front-end commercial capabilities across the region to support future commercialization of differentiated Oncology assets. Site-level environmental capex: renewable-energy Power Purchase Agreements (PPA) implemented at the Nashik and CSN sites, and a transition from fossil fuel to biofuel for boiler operations at the Indore site.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global medicines market projected to grow at 5-8% CAGR through 2030 (exceeding USD 2.6 Tn), supported by sustained innovation despite pricing pressures, healthcare reforms and a significant patent expiry wave; the U.S. is expected to remain the largest contributor to global pharmaceutical market growth.
- Oncology is expected to remain the largest therapy area by spending (8-10% CAGR 2026-2030); Obesity is projected to be the fastest-growing therapy area (13-14% CAGR) on GLP-1 adoption; Immunology, Ophthalmology and CNS are also flagged as continuing growth areas relevant to Glenmark's core therapy exposure.
- India is expected to remain among the world's fastest-growing major economies (GDP +6.6% in FY2027); reduction in GST rates is expected to support consumer spending even as elevated energy prices and input costs moderate private demand.
- Indian pharmaceutical market: domestic market valued at USD 60 Bn, projected to reach USD 130 Bn by FY2030; India supplies around 20% of the world's generic medicines and ~60% of UNICEF's vaccine requirements; government PLI Schemes and the Bulk Drug Parks Scheme continue to support domestic manufacturing capability.
- India business demand: underlying demand profile remained strong through FY2026 despite a pronounced one-time sales impact in Q2 FY2026 from the GST regime change; India formulation business significantly outperformed the IPM in secondary sales every quarter, with sustained strength in Cardiac, Dermatology and Respiratory, growing at ~1.5x IPM growth and ranking as the second-fastest-growing company among the top 15 in FY2026.
- North America growth driver: increasing focus on Respiratory, Injectables and institutional products where complexity and execution can differentiate, supported by continued progress in strengthening manufacturing and supply capabilities, including the Monroe, North Carolina facility's FDA clearance to restart commercial manufacturing.
- Europe growth driver: evolution toward greater contribution from branded and differentiated products, illustrated by the progress of Winlevi® and continued expansion of Ryaltris® across established commercial infrastructure.
- Emerging Markets growth driver: broad commercial footprint, local market understanding and longstanding customer relationships supporting expansion of both Glenmark-originated and partnered therapies.
- IGI multispecific/proprietary pipeline: ISB 2001 (ABBV-2001, licensed to AbbVie) for Oncology and autoimmune disease; next-wave programs referenced include ISB 880 (LAD191) in Immunology, and partnered programs Telazorlimab (ISB 830) and ISB 830-X8 (STAR-0310).
- Oncology partnered/in-licensed pipeline: Tevimbra® (Tislelizumab), Brukinsa® (Zanubrutinib), Aumolertinib, Trastuzumab Rezetecan, Envafolimab, and Akynzeo® (Netupitant/Palonosetron) for cancer supportive care.
- Dermatology partnered pipeline: Winlevi® (Clascoterone) and Jabryus® (Abrocitinib) for Atopic Dermatitis.
- Respiratory partnered pipeline: Pulmicort® (Budesonide) for Asthma/COPD, Eklira® (Aclidinium Bromide) and Duaklir® (Aclidinium Bromide and Formoterol Fumarate Dihydrate).

deepdive.thesis: Glenmark Pharmaceuticals is a global specialty pharma company that discovers, manufactures, and markets branded generics and innovative medicines focused on oncology, respiratory, and dermatology, with strong presence in India and regulated markets.

open.item: Board of Directors recommended a dividend of 250% (₹2.5 per equity share of face value ₹1 each) for FY2026, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM, with total cash outflow of approximately ₹705.50 million.
Glenmark has submitted marketing authorization applications for Aumolertinib across 10 markets, with the first commercial launch anticipated during the second half of FY2027.
Glenmark secured regulatory approval to launch Ryaltris® in Brazil, with the launch planned in FY2027.
IGI is targeting one IND (Investigational New Drug) filing every year from FY2027, progressing the next generation of IGI assets towards clinical development.
The UK launch and EU marketing authorization of Winlevi® provides a platform for further expansion across Glenmark's licensed European territories in FY2027.
Glenmark is targeting over 70% revenue contribution from branded markets by FY2030.

IGI's exclusive licensing agreement with AbbVie for ISB 2001 carries a potential aggregate deal value of USD 1.925 Bn (of which USD 700 Mn upfront has been received) plus tiered double-digit royalties on net sales, with Glenmark leading commercialization across Emerging Markets.
Glenmark is targeting 13–15% revenue CAGR over the medium term, driven by increasing contribution from branded and differentiated businesses.
Glenmark is targeting a Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) above 23%, while maintaining a net cash position.
Glenmark is targeting a Return on Equity (ROE) above 20%.
Glenmark is targeting a 35% reduction in absolute Scope 1 and 2 emissions and a 28% reduction in Scope 3 emissions intensity by 2035.
Glenmark is advancing towards carbon neutrality by 2030 through renewable energy, energy efficiency, and responsible resource management.
